_comment: Layer 0. Store-wide metrics from ShopifyQL, for the overview at the top of the dashboard. Queries and formulas are config, not code: adding a metric or changing a filter is an edit here, never a deploy of new logic.
_VERIFIED: Every query and window below was run against the live First Day store on 2026-09-10 and returned rows. ShopifyQL is read-only aggregated reporting.

filters.newCustomerOnlineStore: new_or_returning_customer = 'New' AND is_canceled_order = false AND sales_channel = 'Online Store' AND excludes_post_order_adjustments = true
filters._comment: Reused across every window so the three numbers are genuinely comparable. The subscription filter is the acquisition filter plus one clause, so the opt-in numerator and denominator share an identical base. subscription_or_one_time takes the values 'subscription' and 'one_time', lowercase.
filters.newCustomerOnlineStoreSubscription: new_or_returning_customer = 'New' AND is_canceled_order = false AND sales_channel = 'Online Store' AND excludes_post_order_adjustments = true AND subscription_or_one_time = 'subscription'
filters.newCustomerOnlineStoreOneTime: new_or_returning_customer = 'New' AND is_canceled_order = false AND sales_channel = 'Online Store' AND excludes_post_order_adjustments = true AND subscription_or_one_time = 'one_time'

windows._comment: The primary window is the number shown; the rest are what it is compared against, nearest first. A window is either a named range (DURING yesterday) or explicit SINCE/UNTIL bounds; DURING replaces both and must not be combined with either. `days` puts TOTALS on a per-day footing before comparing, which a rate does not need.

sessions._comment: The closed funnel, per the sessions schema: sessions, cart additions, reached checkout, completed checkout. These are session counts, not order counts, so they do not tie to the sales schema figures above.

queries._comment: A query is run once per window. The collector assembles FROM <schema> SHOW <show> WHERE <filter> SINCE <since> UNTIL <until>.

subscription._comment: The numerator for Sub. Opt-In. Deliberately NOT a GROUP BY subscription_or_one_time: an order containing both a subscription line and a one-time line appears in both groups, so the groups sum to 12,968 against 9,902 distinct orders. Dividing by that sum understates opt-in by about 18 points.

oneTime._comment: Only used to reconstruct the mix denominator the Shopify report's stacked bar uses, so both readings of opt-in can be shown side by side.

net_aov.label: ncAOV
net_aov._comment: New-customer net AOV. Discounts come back NEGATIVE from ShopifyQL, so adding them subtracts them: gross + discounts + shipping is net revenue, over order count. This is deliberately not Shopify's built-in average_order_value, which is computed on a different base and reads about a dollar lower.
net_aov.description: New Customer AOV. (gross sales + discounts + shipping charges) / orders, for new customers on the Online Store, excluding cancelled orders and post-order adjustments. Discounts arrive negative from ShopifyQL, so adding them subtracts them. This is deliberately not Shopify's built-in average_order_value, which is computed on a different base and reads about a dollar lower.

sub_optin.label: Sub. Opt-In
sub_optin.description: New Customer Subscription Opt-in. The share of distinct new-customer orders that contain a subscription line: subscription orders over the same order count ncAOV is built on, so both tiles describe one population. NOTE this differs from the Shopify report's stacked bar, which groups by subscription_or_one_time. An order containing both a subscription line and a one-time line is counted in BOTH groups, so the groups sum to more than the number of orders and the bar's share is lower. Both figures are shown here: 'of orders' is this tile, 'of mix' is what the report shows. Neither is wrong; they answer different questions. Of orders: did this customer opt in at all. Of mix: what share of the subscription/one-time split is subscription.

sub_mix.label: Sub. mix
sub_mix.description: The subscription share of the subscription/one-time split, matching the stacked bar in the Shopify report. Lower than Sub. Opt-In because an order containing both kinds of line is counted in both halves of the split.
sub_mix._comment: Not a tile by default. It is surfaced in the Sub. Opt-In info hover so the two readings can be compared. Promote it to a tile if the mix view is the one that should lead.

_comment_kind: kind is how a metric may be compared across windows of different lengths. A 'rate' (an average or a ratio) is already normalized and compares directly. A 'total' is not: MTD gross sales against a 7 day total measures the length of the window, not the business, so totals are compared per day. Discounts are goodDirection up because the value is negative, so a rise is less discounting.

alerts._comment: A tile moving more than this against the named window is flagged in the readout. Deliberately blunt: this is a sanity check that the store has not moved under a test, not a statistical claim. Layer 3 owns the statistics.

funnel.label: Conversion funnel
funnel._comment: Each step shows its count, its share of the step above (where the drop-off is) and its share of all sessions. Comparisons are on the STEP RATE, not the count: a window of a different length has a different number of sessions, so only the conversion between steps is comparable across windows.
